changes: Create kernels/custom_ops.cu with a GroupNorm kernel using a two-pass reduction (mean/variance) followed by normalization, or a single-pass Welford with global memory? Two-pass is simpler and accurate enough for atol/rtol 1e-2.
Use float for all arithmetic; compute per (batch, group) mean and variance over all elements in that group.

Store per-(batch,group) mean/var in temporary global buffers allocated by the launcher. The launcher will allocate temporary memory using cudaMalloc, perform reduction with grid-stride loop and shared-memory reduction, then launch normalization, then free temporary memory.

Kernel launch parameters: for reduction, one block per (batch, group), block size 256, each thread processes multiple elements using grid-stride within the block? Actually use a single block per (batch, group) with a grid-stride loop inside the block? For 1024*1024 = 1M elements per group, a single block may be inefficient but acceptable. Alternatively use multi-block two-stage reduction. For simplicity and correctness, use one block per group with block size 1024 max? CUDA max threads per block is 1024. 1M elements with 1024 threads -> ~1024 iterations per thread, fine. Block reduction via shared memory. This avoids allocating extra buffers; we can compute mean/var in one kernel and write directly to temporary arrays (mean, var) of size N*num_groups. Then normalization kernel reads mean/var.
Boundary checks: group size may not be divisible by block size; handle remainder.
